![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14058551/assets/2c633342d5dc1ddb1244d492d81b6b9c00ffe33858398a72acb2a73467d93bb0.png)

The graph of the function $g(x)$ is shown above. 
Find the approximate ${g}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=4$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=2.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=2$ and $x=4.$*

${g}^{′}(4)≈$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{g}^{′}(x)≈\frac{g(x)-g(x-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $x=4.$ Applying the above formula with $x=4$ and $h=2$ gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(4) & ≈\frac{g(4)-g(4-2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{g(4)-g(2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{5-1}{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
